inputs.quality_scope: Fixed representative development users; includes idle users and all release windows.
inputs.accounting_scope: Shared calibration independent of quality sample; population cost is fixed real30k event shapes.

quality.aggregation: Mean of per-release candidate-minus-Reuse AUC differences divided by mean once-rebuild-minus-Reuse differences. All releases retained; not mean recovery percentages.

cost.role: Exact analytic real30k lazy-code event-shape ledger, verified against the executed eight-user eager/lazy probe; not all-population GPU quality or latency.

encoder.scope: Each head's old K/V plus the complete Current item embedding. Query and code-storage costs stay unchanged; per-row encoding is charged at the expanded input width.

cost.denominator: First-request-triggered complete history rebuild once per user per release, plus native service, minus matched Reuse native service.
cost.state_accounting: Bind release parameters without materializing codes; native writes and support always advance. Encode the current retained rows at the first actual request, then arriving rows until the next release or causal retirement. No request prediction, label use, or denominator change.
cost.projection_scope: Same model, three-release horizon and per-resident real-event mix. Fixed calibration population. Extrapolated FLOPs only, not measured quality or service.
cost.initialization_latency_scope: First-request code preparation is additional critical-path work; the separate eight-user probe measured it. These FLOPs do not establish loaded-service latency.

notes: Scoring accepts no labels; labels and frozen reference scores are attached after inference.
Native K/V writes are unchanged and the trajectory is not reset across releases.
The cost denominator and fixed calibration do not shrink when --max-users is used.
Small-sample recovery is a development signal, not acceptance or final generalization.
